params.topic: MLS 2018-2020 only: fill the remaining per-fixture competition-cycle facts needed for Shadow Q+F+I and Q+F+I+M
questions: Only process MLS regular-season fixtures in seasons 2018, 2019 and 2020. Exclude playoffs, MLS Cup, USL, MLS Next Pro, cups, friendlies and any fixture already complete in the local ledger.

Use the local stable_match_key join key season + local date + home_team + away_team. For every locally unresolved row, seek directly evidenced meeting_number, second_cycle, return_leg, cycle_route and official_round/matchday when available. Return only missing or conflicting rows; do not repeat rows already resolved unless needed to show a conflict.

Prefer official MLS schedule/MLS Fact and Record Book or official schedule pages. Cross-check with a complete explicit schedule source such as FBref, WorldFootball or Soccerway. A field derived from a complete schedule is allowed only when the response states field_semantics=derived_from_complete_source_schedule, gives the derivation_rule, ordered source rows or an auditable locator, and source URL. Never infer from partial lists, odds, standings, result order, or row index.

Verify the season-level competition rule for 2018, 2019 and 2020: double_round_robin true/false/unknown, definition, expected schedule rule, and whether it supports mapping second_cycle or return_leg. Preserve NULL for unbalanced schedules, third meetings, same-venue repeat meetings, or unsupported rows.

Return row-level data even when unresolved. Each row must contain stable_match_key, season, date, home_team, away_team, field_name, value or NULL, status (ok/unavailable/blocked/conflict/parse_failed), source_url, final_url, retrieved_at, field_locator, source_sha256 when available, field_semantics, and evidence_notes. Include audit totals and unresolved_queue by season and field.

This is football evidence only. Do not return Qimen charts, palaces, relations, model directions, odds structures, probabilities, Miss labels, Outcome, Review, Gold, or SQLite writes. Do not claim that a field is complete merely because an endpoint exists.
